Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Helios really liked the latency and cost controls you showed. We're starting to scope a Dedicated capacity engagement and need a quick sizing estimate to take to our infra planning team. Attached is a small sample of our QPS traces and a short breakdown of expected prompt/response lengths. High level: we expect production launch in Q1, initial traffic profile below.

- Typical steady-state QPS: 12 requests/sec (text-gen API)
- 95th percentile concurrency target: 60 concurrent sessions (conservative headroom)
- Prompt distribution: median 180 tokens, 95th 420 tokens
- Response distribution: median 120 tokens, 95th 780 tokens
- Burst scenario: sustained 3 minute spikes up to 75 QPS during reporting windows (~3x baseline)
- Latency SLO: 95% <= 220ms tail for short prompts (~<256 tokens); degrade gracefully for longer responses
- Model: planning to use an LLM comparable to the opensource Helios-2.7b (kv-cache friendly) — will consider quantized variants

Questions we'd like you to answer in the sizing:
1) Recommended GPU SKUs and counts to meet the steady-state + burst with 99% availability
2) Suggested batching/kv-cache settings to preserve SLO while minimizing GPU count
3) Any recommendations on quantization or model variants for cost/latency tradeoffs
4) Estimated monthly token cost and rough request concurrency headroom per GPU

I've attached a sample CSV (helios_sample_traffic.csv) with 24h of anonymized traces. Let me know if you need extra signals (e.g., session stickiness, top-k sampling params). Can we block 30 minutes this week for a short sizing sync?

Thanks,
Alex

Looping you both in — forwarding the Helios traffic sample and Karthik's clarifying notes. My quick read (will validate against the CSV):

Preliminary mapping notes (ballpark, before run):
- If 12 QPS is pure text-gen with the token distribution listed, estimate ~= 6–8 A100-80GB equivalents for steady-state (assuming medium batching & KV caching) to hit 95% < 220ms on short prompts.
- For burst headroom to 75 QPS for ~3 minutes, propose ability to autoscale an additional 2–4 SKUs (or allow overflow to hosted fallback) — dedicated-only config should size for steady + autoscale buffer.
- For cost-sensitive deploy, recommend testing 4-bit quantized weights (int4/fp8 hybrid) for the Helios-2.7b variant — yields 1.8–2.5x inference throughput per GPU in our internal tests with <2% quality delta on generation metrics.
- Batching: dynamic batching with a 12ms batch window and request-level early flush for short prompts usually balances latency vs GPU utilization.
- Cache: prefix + session KV cache for returning sessions; TTL 30m default — reduces per-request token compute significantly for multi-turn flows.

Action items for sizing run:
1) Karthik — run the trace through the estimator (include per-model perf profile for Helios-2.7b quantized and FP16).
2) Dev — can you produce a quick mapping of token/sec to GPU count for L4 vs A10G vs A100 SKUs for the given distributions?
3) I'll draft two packaging options (Conservative: dedicated-only with autoscale buffer; Cost-first: quantized + more aggressive batching).

Attachments: workload_signature.csv (workload signature extracted from the sample)
